channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 amid US probe into Nvidia chip sales
item.description: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced that former executive Alice Huang departed in August 2025 and holds no current role, defending its operations as lawful. The company purchased billions of dollars in Nvidia chips between 2024 and 2026, prompting a U.S. Commerce Department inquiry into potential export control violations. The investigation highlights heightened scrutiny over global AI chip supply chains and follows the abrupt resignation of Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.

item.title: Jensen Huang discusses Nvidia CEO comeback as allies lobby for return
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly discussed returning to lead the chipmaker with confidants, as allies form a lobbying effort for his reinstatement. Huang resigned following an investigation into personal relationships that involved an executive at Megaspeed. The potential return of a long-standing CEO after a major governance and security scandal impacts leadership stability at the world's most valuable public chipmaker.

item.title: Congress moves to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
item.description: Following revelations regarding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, US lawmakers are pushing for stricter export controls on advanced AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans are reviewing legislative measures and demanding public testimony from industry and government leaders. The political fallout from the Nvidia scandal could accelerate bipartisan efforts to reshape US technology export policies and restrict foreign access to advanced AI hardware.

item.title: Nvidia sought Taipei's help after employee's chip smuggling case
item.description: Nvidia appealed to Taiwanese officials and sought advice from TSMC after an Nvidia manager was charged over helping smuggle AI chips into China. Prosecutors accused the manager of being the core figure in a network that smuggled 74 servers containing Nvidia chips to China. This case highlights the compliance and enforcement challenges companies face regarding the illicit diversion of AI chips to restricted markets.

item.title: US and allies agree to create joint list to protect AI supply chains from China
item.description: The US and allies including Japan, the UK, and India agreed to create a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains to protect from China. The accord comes ahead of Donald Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen. This agreement establishes a coordinated international approach among major economies to secure artificial intelligence supply chains and restrict technology transfer involving China.

item.title: Howard Lutnick joins Trump on Air Force One to China amid Nvidia chip curbs dispute
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to travel on Air Force One with the president to China this week. The trip follows clashes with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and others over Nvidia chip curbs. Internal policy disputes among cabinet members over chip export restrictions can directly affect trade regulations and semiconductor companies.

item.title: Apple plans smart glasses launch in 2027 relying on Siri and iPhone apps
item.description: Apple plans to unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027 and ship them before the end of the year, according to a report by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The glasses will integrate third-party iPhone apps with Siri AI and feature cameras for Visual Intelligence. This details Apple's strategy for entering the smart glasses market by anchoring its wearable device to existing iPhone apps and Siri AI rather than running software natively on the glasses.

item.title: Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip curbs affecting a former firm's client
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip rules that would affect Southeast Asian data centers. Some of these data centers are clients of his former firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, and one may serve Tencent. It shows how government policy on AI chip export restrictions can intersect with the past financial ties of top officials.

item.title: Scott Bessent urges Nvidia leadership shakeup and answers on China chip sales
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a dramatic leadership shakeup at Nvidia following the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. Bessent demanded answers within 10 days on whether Nvidia pushed seemingly illicit chip sales to China to boost revenue. The demands from a cabinet secretary regarding Nvidia's leadership and customer screening signal heightened government scrutiny over AI chip exports and corporate governance.

item.title: Sebi to issue AI usage guidelines for capital markets focusing on investor protection
item.description: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced that the regulator will soon release detailed guidelines governing AI use in securities markets, emphasizing disclosures, accountability and a human‑in‑the‑loop approach to protect investors. The rules aim to safeguard market integrity and investor interests as AI tools become more prevalent in trading and analysis.

item.title: Nvidia faces earnings scrutiny amid leadership change and stock decline
item.description: Nvidia reports its third fiscal quarter earnings on November 17, 2026, with expected revenue of around $109 billion and earnings per share of $2.48. The upcoming earnings call will be run by interim CEO Colette Kress following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang on November 12. Nvidia's financial results and leadership transition mark a pivotal moment for a dominant force in the artificial intelligence hardware market.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following investigation into personal relationships
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following an investigation into personal relationships, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim chief. The departure of the 33-year company veteran leaves the world's most valuable public chipmaker facing a leadership transition. Jensen Huang's departure marks a turning point for Nvidia, which controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for AI computer chips and sits at the center of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Nidus raises $30M to deploy AI robotics in US defense factories
item.description: Nidus raised $30 million across pre-seed and seed rounds to deploy AI-powered technology for manufacturing robots in US defense factories. The startup reported over $1 million in early customer bookings or revenue within its first four months. This funding highlights growing venture capital investment in applying physical AI and foundation robotics models to constrained manufacturing sectors like defense.

item.title: TSMC plans $500M fund to invest in chip startups and suppliers
item.description: TSMC plans to use a new $500 million venture fund to invest in chip startups, suppliers, and other upstream partners. Senior executive Kevin Zhang stated the company wants to support future chip titans during the AI boom. The investment fund highlights how major semiconductor manufacturers are positioning themselves to capture growth across the broader AI chip supply chain.

item.title: Nebuly raises $21M Series A to measure business value of AI agents
item.description: Nebuly has raised a $21 million Series A funding round to expand its platform that measures the return on investment of enterprise AI agents. The Turin-based company connects to custom-built agents and assistants from providers such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot to analyze their impact on productivity and revenue. As enterprises face rising AI bills and pressure from boards to prove return on investment, tools that move beyond basic usage metrics like prompt counts to measure actual business value are gaining venture backing.

item.title: Nvidia chips accessed by Chinese companies in SE Asia data centers
item.description: Massive data centers in Southeast Asia exploited a gap in U.S. sanctions to provide computing power for Chinese companies using Nvidia AI chips. This backdoor route built a multibillion-dollar business that kept Beijing in the AI race. It shows how export controls can be bypassed through overseas data center networks, affecting regulatory strategies for AI hardware.

item.title: Democrats launch inquiry into Nvidia chip sales and Trump administration policies
item.description: Congressional Democrats launched an inquiry into the Trump administration's handling of Nvidia chip sales to China and export licenses. The investigation follows the ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid a scandal connecting company leadership, government officials, and foreign shipments. The investigation ties corporate AI chip manufacturing and export policies directly to federal oversight and political debate.

item.title: Ethan Mollick creates SatBench to track AI benchmark saturation
item.description: Ethan Mollick created SatBench to measure how quickly major AI benchmarks become saturated by AI, finding that 63% of 173 benchmarks cited by labs since 2023 are now saturated. It highlights that AI models are improving at a pace that outruns traditional methods of measurement.

item.title: Nvidia risks losing supply chain deals without Jensen Huang, warns Elon Musk
item.description: Elon Musk warned that Nvidia could lose critical supply chain agreements following the departure of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while searching for a successor. The departure of Nvidia's longtime CEO and potential loss of informal supply chain agreements introduce operational uncertainty for a central supplier of artificial intelligence chips.

item.title: Nvidia investors urge board to keep Jensen Huang return option open
item.description: Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management CIO Gavin Baker wrote to Nvidia's board urging a slow, measured succession process and to keep the door open for founder Jensen Huang to return as CEO. The investors, who hold $2.13 billion in Nvidia stock, expressed confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress. Board decisions on leadership will shape Nvidia's strategic direction and impact the broader AI ecosystem.

item.title: Databento raises $100M Series C at $1.1B valuation
item.description: Market data platform Databento raised a $100 million Series C round at a $1.1 billion valuation, led by Fifth Down Capital. The company reports it has doubled its revenue since its Series B round and holds enterprise contracts with five of the six largest frontier AI labs. The funding highlights the growing demand for programmatic, cloud-delivered market data from both traditional financial institutions and frontier AI labs.

item.title: Nvidia open-source strategy questioned following Jensen Huang's resignation
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, leaving Colette Kress to take over as interim chief. His departure raises questions about Nvidia's future support for open-source AI initiatives, open-weight models, and related startup investments. Jensen Huang was a major advocate and financier for open-source AI, and his departure threatens the funding and advocacy that supported open-source developers.

item.title: Ethan Mollick on agent swarm research traffic and Fable 5.2
item.description: Ethan Mollick reported that agent swarms conducting research generate large volumes of traffic and use repeated full-text searches to find information. He used Claude Fable 5.2 to reconstruct W.H. Auden's 1941 poetry class by having it read an obscure book from the Internet Archive line by line. It highlights the practical capabilities of AI agent swarms in performing complex, multi-step research tasks and the resulting impact on web traffic.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns as Colette Kress takes over as interim chief
item.description: NVIDIA co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned following an admission regarding a personal relationship, with CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO. The leadership change has triggered market concerns and raised questions about the company's future strategy on open-source AI and international projects. Jensen Huang's departure removes a central figure who shaped NVIDIA's market dominance, open-source advocacy, and global infrastructure footprint, leaving the company's future direction subject to uncertainty under interim leadership.

item.title: MeitY opens DPDP Act consent manager registration portal
item.description: MeitY launched an online portal for companies to register as consent managers under the DPDP Act, 2023, requiring a minimum net worth of ₹2 crore. The framework came into effect on November 13, 2026. This marks a key step in operationalising India's data protection framework, allowing certified entities to offer consent management services while giving individuals more control over their personal data.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid scandals, ending an era for Big Tech
item.description: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned following admissions of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, and chip smuggling scandals. Around 60 employees reported directly to Huang, who had no designated successor. The departure of Big Tech's last prominent visionary founder CEO introduces uncertainty regarding Nvidia's market dominance, support for open-source AI, and future leadership direction.

item.title: Nvidia faces leadership transition and market shifts after Jensen Huang's exit
item.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO following revelations about personal relationships, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. Nvidia shares fell 4.34% to $166.19 following the resignation, while competitor AMD shares rose 5.86%. Huang's departure removes a central figure in the AI ecosystem and open-source advocacy, shifting competitive dynamics for rivals like AMD and Google.

item.title: Jensen Huang struggled to access Beijing chip policymakers
item.description: Sources report that despite over 20 years of business in China, former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang struggled to gain access to policymakers driving Beijing's chip self-sufficiency campaign. It highlights the complex geopolitical and access barriers faced by major U.S. chip executives navigating Beijing's domestic technology initiatives.

item.title: WhiteMatter raises $20 million Series A for AI agent governance platform
item.description: Cybersecurity startup WhiteMatter raised a $20 million Series A funding round led by Blumberg Capital, bringing its total funding to $24 million. The company builds platform governance and "guardian" agents to oversee AI agent file access, software use, and decision-making. As enterprises deploy millions of autonomous AI agents across endpoints and cloud environments, security startups are emerging to monitor, govern, and control agent behavior at scale.

item.title: Sam Bankman-Fried misses out on Anthropic IPO windfall
item.description: An analysis shows that Sam Bankman-Fried's 2021 investment of $500M in Anthropic would be worth approximately $37B if the company lists at a $1.5T valuation. However, the jailed cryptocurrency mogul relinquished his stake in 2024 for about $1.3B. It highlights the massive scale of potential returns from early-stage AI investments and the impact of liquidation timing for distressed estates.
